─────────────────────────────────────────────
OVERVIEW
─────────────────────────────────────────────

This brief covers seven rule changes derived from gap analysis showing systematic extraction failures across four categories: strain/compound provenance conflation, exposure-method misfires in ex vivo and aquatic contexts, dietary-delivery misclassification as edibles, and dose field imputation errors. All seven changes are required to move alignment above the 80% threshold. Changes are ordered high-priority first.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
CHANGE 1 — strain_reported: DUAL-TARGET EXTRACTION
File: extractor.py | Priority: HIGH
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: strain_reported currently attempts one extraction pass looking for animal catalog strings (e.g., Sprague-Dawley, C57BL/6, JAX colony numbers). For pure-cannabinoid studies that source compound from a chemical vendor, the field returns null or incorrectly inherits an irrelevant string. Claude returns the compound provenance string (compound name + vendor + purity) in these cases, creating 100% disagreement on the strain_reported field for that paper subset.

Implementation:

Split the extraction function into two sequential sub-extractors operating on the full abstract and any available methods text.

Sub-extractor A — Animal strain/vendor: retain all existing patterns for JAX, Envigo, Charles River, Harlan, Taconic, and common inbred/outbred strain designators (Sprague-Dawley, Wistar, C57BL/6, BALB/c, CD-1, Long-Evans, etc.). This runs first. If a match is found, assign it and skip sub-extractor B.

Sub-extractor B — Compound provenance: activated only when (a) cannabis_type resolves to 'pure cannabinoid' AND (b) sub-extractor A returns null. Build a pattern that captures: compound name (THC, CBD, cannabidiol, delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol, CBG, CBDV, etc.) followed within 0–80 characters by any of: Sigma-Aldrich, Cayman Chemical, Tocris, NIDA Drug Supply Program, THC Pharm, Lipomed, or a purity expression (greater-than N%, NNN mg/mL, certified reference). Concatenate the matched compound name, vendor name, and purity string into strain_reported separated by a semicolon. Example output: "CBD; Cayman Chemical; >98% purity".

If neither sub-extractor fires, return null explicitly rather than an empty string.

maude_cues.json additions: add a "compound_provenance_vendors" key containing the vendor list above so it can be maintained without touching extractor.py. Add a "animal_strain_patterns" key enumerating the catalog phrases currently hardcoded, making them patchable.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
CHANGE 2 — exposure_method: DISSOLVED IN MEDIA CLASS + INJECTION GUARD
File: extractor.py | Priority: HIGH
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: The injection classifier fires on any administration-adjacent language, including ex vivo tissue bath descriptions and zebrafish embryo immersion protocols. "Animals were injected with vehicle" appearing in a paper that primarily uses tissue strips is tagging the paper as injection, overriding the correct route.

Implementation:

Step 1 — Add explicit detection block for dissolved-in-media route. Before any injection detection runs, scan full text for any of the following trigger phrases: "isolated...strips", "isolated tissue", "tissue bath", "organ bath", "bath application", "embryos were exposed to", "tank water contained", "immersion in", "dissolved in artificial cerebrospinal fluid", "superfusion". If any trigger fires, set exposure_method to "cannabinoids dissolved in media" and return immediately — do not continue to injection detection.

Step 2 — Restrict injection detection to hard route abbreviations only. The injection branch may only fire if at least one of the following explicit strings is present: "i.p.", "i.v.", "s.c.", "subcutaneous", "intraperitoneal", "intravenous", "intrathecal", "intracerebroventricular", "i.c.v.". Remove any broader "inject" stem matching (inject*, injection) that is not accompanied by one of these abbreviations or spelled-out route names.

Step 3 — Add "oral gavage" and "gavage" as a distinct exposure_method value if either word appears and no dissolved-in-media trigger is active.

maude_cues.json additions: add "dissolved_in_media_triggers" array and "injection_route_guards" array so both lists are configurable.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
CHANGE 3 — cannabis_type: GUARD AGAINST EDIBLES MIS-TAG FOR DIETARY COMPOUNDS
File: maude_classifier.py | Priority: HIGH
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: Pure compound (THC, CBD) mixed into rodent chow or gelatin pellets is being tagged cannabis_type='edibles' because the classifier detects a dietary delivery context. The correct tag is 'pure cannabinoid' because the substance is a chemically defined compound sourced from a verified supplier, not an edible cannabis product.

Implementation:

In the cannabis_type classification function in maude_classifier.py, after any initial label is assigned, run a vendor/purity override check. If the text associated with the compound description contains any of: Sigma-Aldrich, Cayman, Tocris, NIDA Drug Supply, THC Pharm, Lipomed, or a purity expression pattern (r'\d+\.?\d*\s*%\s*purity' or r'certified reference standard'), override cannabis_type to 'pure cannabinoid' regardless of the delivery vehicle. This override must fire even if words like 'chow', 'diet', 'food', 'pellet', 'cookie', or 'brownie' are also present, because the decisive criterion is compound identity, not delivery form.

Separately, tighten the edibles detection to require at least one explicit product phrase: 'cannabis-infused', 'edible product', 'cannabis edible', 'brownie', 'cookie', 'cannabis cookie', 'infused brownie'. Generic dietary words alone must not trigger the edibles tag.

Update maude_cues.json: add "edibles_required_phrases" array (the explicit product strings above) and "pure_cannabinoid_vendor_override" array (the vendor/purity strings) to keep classification logic data-driven.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
CHANGE 4 — duration_days: BROADEN REGEX AND ADD WEEK CONVERSION
File: extractor.py | Priority: HIGH
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: Duration extraction only fires on Methods-section header context. Many abstracts state duration inline ("Animals were treated for 14 days", "following a 28-day protocol") without section headers. Week expressions are also not converted.

Implementation:

Replace the existing single pattern with a cascade of three patterns applied to the full available text (abstract + methods if present), taking the first non-null result in priority order:

Pattern 1 — explicit day count in treatment context: r'(?:for|following|after)\s+(\d+)\s+days?\b' and r'(\d+)[- ]day\s+(?:treatment|exposure|protocol|administration|regimen)'. Capture group is the integer day count.

Pattern 2 — days of treatment phrasing: r'(\d+)\s+days?\s+of\s+(?:treatment|exposure|administration)'. Capture group is the integer day count.

Pattern 3 — week expression fallback: r'(?:for|following)\s+(\d+)\s+weeks?\b' and r'(\d+)[- ]week\s+(?:treatment|exposure|protocol)'. Multiply captured integer by 7 and store as duration_days. Add a boolean flag duration_from_weeks=True in the extraction metadata to signal downstream reconciliation that this is a derived value.

When full PDF is available and yields a conflicting week count, prefer the PDF value over the abstract-derived value. Log both for audit.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
CHANGE 5 — cbd_mg_kg / thc_mg_kg: PARSE PER-DAY QUALIFIER
File: extractor.py | Priority: HIGH
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: Dose expressions written as "10 mg/kg/day" or "10 mg/kg per day" are not being captured because the current regex requires exactly "mg/kg" with no trailing qualifier. The per-day suffix causes a non-match.

Implementation:

Update the dose regex to: r'(\d+\.?\d*)\s*mg/kg(?:\s*/\s*day|/day|\s+per\s+day)?' making the per-day qualifier optional with the trailing ? so both "mg/kg" and "mg/kg/day" and "mg/kg per day" all match and populate the same numeric field.

After capturing the numeric value, assign it to thc_mg_kg or cbd_mg_kg based on compound context: scan the sentence containing the match for THC synonyms (THC, delta-9-THC, delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol, Δ9-THC) to assign thc_mg_kg, or CBD synonyms (CBD, cannabidiol) to assign cbd_mg_kg. If both appear in the same sentence (combination study), populate both fields with the same value only if the sentence clearly applies the dose to both; otherwise flag for manual review.

maude_cues.json: add "thc_synonyms" and "cbd_synonyms" arrays used by this context-assignment logic.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
CHANGE 6 — administration_frequency: REMOVE FALLBACK DEFAULT
File: extractor.py | Priority: MEDIUM
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: When no frequency keyword is found in text, extractor.py returns 'once daily' as a default. This invented value propagates into downstream analyses and was confirmed to disagree with Claude's null return in papers where frequency was genuinely unstated.

Implementation:

Remove any fallback default assignment in the administration_frequency extraction function. The function must return null (Python None, serialized as JSON null) when no frequency keyword is detected.

Recognized frequency values and their normalized forms: 'daily' → 'daily', 'once daily' → 'daily', 'once per day' → 'daily', 'twice daily' → 'twice daily', 'bid' → 'twice daily', 'three times daily' → 'three times daily', 'tid' → 'three times daily', 'every other day' → 'every other day', 'X times per week' → 'X times per week', 'X days per week' → 'X days per week', 'every N days' → 'every N days', 'weekly' → 'weekly'.

Do not normalize 'daily' and 'once daily' as equivalent — both should map to the single canonical string 'daily'. No other normalization collapse is permitted. If frequency appears multiple times in text with different values (e.g., escalating dose schedule), return an array of the distinct values and set a multi_frequency flag.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
CHANGE 7 — dose_mg: REMOVE WEIGHT-MULTIPLICATION INFERENCE
File: extractor.py | Priority: MEDIUM
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: When only a mg/kg dose is present, extractor.py back-calculates an absolute dose_mg using an assumed animal body weight (30g mouse, 300g rat). This is methodologically incorrect — assumed weight is not ground truth — and produced confirmed errors of 60mg and 180mg in papers 13048 and 13570.

Implementation:

Remove all body-weight multiplication logic from the dose_mg extraction path. dose_mg must only be populated when the source text contains an explicit absolute dose expression: 'X mg per animal', 'X mg total dose', 'X mg injected', or a numeric mg value that is not qualified by /kg or /kg/day. If the text gives only mg/kg, populate thc_mg_kg or cbd_mg_kg (per Change 5) and leave dose_mg as null.

Add a source_is_absolute boolean to the extraction output that is True only when an unqualified mg expression was found. This allows downstream validation to distinguish clean absolute doses from null-due-to-inference.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
maude_cues.json — CONSOLIDATED KEY ADDITIONS
─────────────────────────────────────────────

The following keys should be added or created if the file does not already contain them. All are arrays of strings unless noted.

compound_provenance_vendors — vendor names for sub-extractor B in Change 1
animal_strain_patterns — catalog strain strings currently hardcoded in extractor.py
dissolved_in_media_triggers — tissue bath and aquatic immersion phrases for Change 2
injection_route_guards — explicit route abbreviations and spellings for Change 2
edibles_required_phrases — mandatory phrases for edibles classification in Change 3
pure_cannabinoid_vendor_override — vendor/purity strings triggering override in Change 3
thc_synonyms — THC compound name variants for Change 5
cbd_synonyms — CBD compound name variants for Change 5

─────────────────────────────────────────────
TEST IDEAS
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Test 1 — strain_reported dual target: Feed a pure-cannabinoid paper abstract containing "CBD obtained from Cayman Chemical (>98% purity)" with no animal strain mention. Assert strain_reported equals "CBD; Cayman Chemical; >98% purity". Feed a rodent paper with "C57BL/6 mice (Jackson Laboratories)". Assert strain_reported equals the JAX string and sub-extractor B did not fire.

Test 2 — exposure_method dissolved-in-media guard: Feed abstract containing "isolated aortic strips were incubated with 10 µM CBD". Assert exposure_method equals "cannabinoids dissolved in media". Feed zebrafish abstract "embryos were exposed to THC in tank water". Assert same value. Verify neither triggers injection class.

Test 3 — exposure_method injection guard: Feed abstract "Rats received i.p. injections of THC (5 mg/kg)". Assert exposure_method equals "injection". Feed abstract with only the word "injected" and no route abbreviation. Assert exposure_method is not "injection" — should be null or require a separate route to resolve.

Test 4 — cannabis_type edibles override: Feed text "THC (Sigma-Aldrich, >99% purity) was incorporated into standard rodent chow". Assert cannabis_type equals "pure cannabinoid". Feed text "rats received cannabis-infused brownies". Assert cannabis_type equals "edibles".

Test 5 — duration_days week conversion: Feed "Animals were treated for 6 weeks". Assert duration_days equals 42 and duration_from_weeks flag is True. Feed "following a 28-day protocol". Assert duration_days equals 28 and flag is False.

Test 6 — dose per day parsing: Feed "CBD (10 mg/kg/day) was administered by gavage". Assert cbd_mg_kg equals 10.0. Feed "THC at 5 mg/kg per day". Assert thc_mg_kg equals 5.0. Feed "vehicle or CBD (20 mg/kg)". Assert cbd_mg_kg equals 20.0 (no per-day qualifier required).

Test 7 — administration_frequency no default: Feed abstract with no frequency language. Assert administration_frequency is null. Feed "once daily gavage". Assert value is "daily". Feed "injections every other day". Assert "every other day". Confirm "daily" and "once daily" both normalize to "daily".

Test 8 — dose_mg no inference: Feed "THC 5 mg/kg i.p.". Assert dose_mg is null and thc_mg_kg equals 5.0. Feed "each rat received 2 mg THC total". Assert dose_mg equals 2.0 and source_is_absolute is True. Confirm papers 13048 and 13570 now return null for dose_mg rather than 60mg and 180mg.

Test 9 — integration regression: Re-run all papers in the node2b disagreement set after all seven changes are applied. Target: alignment rises from 75.6% to at least 82%. Log any new disagreement fields introduced by the changes so they can be caught in node2c.

Problem: When no frequency keyword is found in text, extractor.py returns 'once daily' as a default. This invented value propagates into downstream analyses and was confirmed to disagree with Claude's null return in papers where frequency was genuinely unstated.

Implementation:

Remove any fallback default assignment in the administration_frequency extraction function. The function must return null (Python None, serialized as JSON null) when no frequency keyword is detected.

Recognized frequency values and their normalized forms: 'daily' → 'daily', 'once daily' → 'daily', 'once per day' → 'daily', 'twice daily' → 'twice daily', 'bid' → 'twice daily', 'three times daily' → 'three times daily', 'tid' → 'three times daily', 'every other day' → 'every other day', 'X times per week' → 'X times per week', 'X days per week' → 'X days per week', 'every N days' → 'every N days', 'weekly' → 'weekly'.

Do not normalize 'daily' and 'once daily' as equivalent — both should map to the single canonical string 'daily'. No other normalization collapse is permitted. If frequency appears multiple times in text with different values (e.g., escalating dose schedule), return an array of the distinct values and set a multi_frequency flag.

CHANGE 7 — dose_mg: REMOVE WEIGHT-MULTIPLICATION INFERENCE
File: extractor.py | Priority: MEDIUM
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: When only a mg/kg dose is present, extractor.py back-calculates an absolute dose_mg using an assumed animal body weight (30g mouse, 300g rat). This is methodologically incorrect — assumed weight is not ground truth — and produced confirmed errors of 60mg and 180mg in papers 13048 and 13570.

Implementation:

Remove all body-weight multiplication logic from the dose_mg extraction path. dose_mg must only be populated when the source text contains an explicit absolute dose expression: 'X mg per animal', 'X mg total dose', 'X mg injected', or a numeric mg value that is not qualified by /kg or /kg/day. If the text gives only mg/kg, populate thc_mg_kg or cbd_mg_kg (per Change 5) and leave dose_mg as null.

Add a source_is_absolute boolean to the extraction output that is True only when an unqualified mg expression was found. This allows downstream validation to distinguish clean absolute doses from null-due-to-inference.
